title: According to the effort (Avot 5:23)
hook: Ben Hei Hei: the reward is according to the effort
tomorrow: if the answer is no, why keep doing the thing at all?

segments.voice: Yesterday, turn it and turn it: everything is in it, and the reader changes each time. Today, the sage right after Ben Bag Bag.

Opening night is done. The bows, the flowers from the lobby, the photos. Then the quiet in the car on the way home, and a question that sneaks in once the applause stops. What if nobody who mattered was watching? Was the work worth it either way? Ben Hei Hei answers in a single short line of Aramaic.
screen: `THE BOWS, THE FLOWERS.` → `THE QUIET CAR.` → `WORTH IT EITHER WAY?`

segments.voice: Ben Hei Hei says: lefum tza'ara agra. According to the effort is the reward. The word tza'ara is effort, and it can also mean pain: what it cost you. Notice what the line leaves out. It doesn't say according to the result. It doesn't say according to who saw. The reward follows the cost, not the scoreboard. That's the life part, for a week like this one: a test you studied for and still did badly on, a job you gave everything and didn't get, a show that went well with no one important in the seats. Ben Hei Hei measures the thing you actually control. And the Talmud gives his name a second scene. There, Bar Hei Hei asks Hillel a question, and Hillel answers that a student who reviews a lesson a hundred times can't be compared to one who reviews it a hundred and one. The extra time is the one that costs. That fits right after yesterday's turn it and turn it. One more turn, when you're tired of turning, is where the reward lives. None of this says results don't matter. It says they aren't the measure.
screen: `LEFUM TZA'ARA AGRA.` · `THE COST, NOT THE SCOREBOARD.` · `A HUNDRED AND ONE TIMES.` · `RESULTS AREN'T THE MEASURE.` · then, large: `ACCORDING TO THE EFFORT.`

segments.voice: Pick one small thing within reach: fold a shirt, straighten a shelf, write your name. Do it now, slowly, with full effort, as if it were the only task of the day. When it's done, rest your hands and notice what the care itself was like.
screen: `ONE SMALL THING.` · `FULL EFFORT, SLOWLY.` · `REST YOUR HANDS.`

segments.voice: According to the effort: Ben Hei Hei's measure for the reward. What it cost, not what it won.
Carry it out the door: according to the effort, not the applause, not the phone call. Good night.

screen: `DAY 1482 COUNTS.` → `AVOT, CHAPTERS 3–6 · 55 OF 60.` → `TOMORROW: IF THE ANSWER IS NO, WHY KEEP DOING THE THING AT ALL?`

howItsDone: Ben Hei Hei's Aramaic line, lefum tza'ara agra, is quoted in Jewish learning as a word of encouragement for hard study or hard work; it is read with chapter five of Avot on summer Shabbat afternoons.

notes: Avot 5:23 paraphrased: Ben Hei Hei says: according to the effort (tza'ara, also pain) is the reward. Confirm translation of tza'ara.

Chagigah 9b: Bar Hei Hei asks Hillel about Malachi 3:18; Hillel answers that one who reviews his chapter a hundred times is not like one who reviews it a hundred and one times. The script assumes Bar Hei Hei and Ben Hei Hei are the same sage (as commonly read); confirm.
Not used: Tosafot's tradition (Chagigah 9b) that Ben Bag Bag and Ben Hei Hei were converts. Could be added later with a Keeper's okay.
